inputs.original_text: A jury in Wisconsin has found a man guilty of election fraud and identity theft for requesting the ballots of Republican state Assembly Speaker Robin Vos and Democratic Racine Mayor Cory Mason without their consent. A Racine County jury on Tuesday found Harry Wait guilty of two misdemeanor election fraud charges and one felony identity theft charge following a two-day trial. He was acquitted of a second count of identity theft. Wait leads a group that makes false election claims. He admitted in 2022 that he requested the ballots to try to prove that the state’s voter registration system is vulnerable to fraud.
inputs.modified_text: They’re using Harry Wait’s convictions to bury the part that matters: he showed how the registration system could be exploited. He requested ballots for Robin Vos and Cory Mason without consent, and the jury convicted him of two misdemeanor election fraud charges and one felony identity theft charge while acquitting him of another identity theft count. That split verdict gives institutions just enough cover to declare the matter settled and brand scrutiny “false election claims.” The message is clear: punish the person who probes the machinery, then let those invested in keeping it unquestioned decide what the public is allowed to ask.
